description: Viewer that boosts available light to show a scene in the dark.
Viewer that shows a scene by the heat it gives off.
Telescope that gathers light with a primary mirror and a flat secondary mirror at the side of the tube; the Dobsonian is a version of it.
Telescope with a sensor and no eyepiece that shows the sky on a screen or app.
Telescope made to observe the Sun in hydrogen-alpha light.
Microscope with its own sensor that shows the image on a screen or computer.
Loupe or magnifier on a headband or clip; also called a binocular loupe.
Glasses with a solar filter made for looking at the Sun.
Mechanical model of the Sun, planets and moons.
Instrument that models the sky for finding the positions of stars and the time.
Projector that shows the night sky on a dome or wall.
Instrument that reads the air temperature indoors or outdoors; a working Galileo thermometer counts here.
Set of instruments that measures several weather quantities together, with a display; sensor count and shielding vary by model.
Instrument that measures pollutants or particles in the air.
Freezer or ultra-low-temperature unit made for cold storage of samples; laboratory refrigerators are included.
Ventilated cabinet that draws fumes from work on samples away from the user.
Kit made to teach science through experiments, sold by subject such as chemistry, physics and electricity, biology, earth and space, or crystals and materials.
Camera made only to fit a telescope.
Camera or adapter made to fit only one kind of microscope.
Tripod made to carry a telescope mount head, sold apart from the mount; a universal photo tripod is in Cameras & Photography.
Instrument that splits light from a sample into a spectrum and measures it (UV-Vis, infrared, Raman, emission); a hand spectroscope counts here.
Small sighting device fitted on a telescope tube to aim it: finderscope, right-angle finder, red-dot or ring sight. The polar scope is listed separately.
Filter for a telescope eyepiece barrel, filter wheel or camera that passes chosen wavelengths (colour, moon, light-pollution, nebula, narrowband); solar filters are listed separately.
Objective lens that screws into a microscope nosepiece (RMS or M25 thread), sold apart from the stand; class and tube-length standard vary.
Eyepiece made for a microscope tube (23.2 or 30 mm and other barrels), sold apart from the stand; wide-field type and power vary.
